title.zh: 卷一百三十一 列傳第六十九: 宦者 梁珫 宋珪 潘守恆 方伎 劉完素 張從正 李慶嗣 紀天錫 張元素 馬貴中 武禎子:亢 李懋 胡德新
title.en: Volume 131 Biographies 69: Huan Zhe, Liang Chong, Song Gui, Pan Shouheng, Fang Ji, Liu Wansu, Zhang Congzheng, Li Qingsi, Ji Tianxi, Zhang Yuansu, Ma Guizhong, Wu Zhen son: Kang, Li Mao, Hu Dexin
title.raw: 卷一百三十一 列傳第六十九: 宦者 梁珫 宋珪 潘守恆 方伎 劉完素 張從正 李慶嗣 紀天錫 張元素 馬貴中 武禎子:亢 李懋 胡德新 Volume 131 Biographies 69: Huan Zhe, Liang Chong, Song Gui, Pan Shouheng, Fang Ji, Liu Wansu, Zhang Congzheng, Li Qingsi, Ji Tianxi, Zhang Yuansu, Ma Guizhong, Wu Zhen son: Kang, Li Mao, Hu Dexin

sentences.zh: 古之宦者皆出於刑人，刑余不可列於士庶，故掌宮寺之事，謂之「婦寺」焉。

translations.literal: In antiquity all eunuchs came from convicts; those mutilated by punishment could not be ranked among gentry and commoners, and therefore managed palace and temple affairs, and were called "inner-chamber attendants" (fushi).
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times every court eunuch sprang from the penal system—men mutilated under criminal sentence could not stand among scholars or commoners, so they were charged with palace and temple affairs and were known as "inner-chamber attendants."

sentences.zh: 東漢以來，宦者養子以繼世。

translations.literal: From the Eastern Han onward, eunuchs adopted sons to continue their line.
translations.idiomatic: From the Eastern Han on, eunuchs took adopted sons to carry on their households.

sentences.zh: 唐世，繼者皆為閹人，其初進也，性多巧慧便僻、善固恩寵，及其得志，黨比糾結不可制。

translations.literal: In the Tang era, successors were all castrated men; when they first entered service, their nature was mostly clever, artful, and skilled at securing favor, and once they attained their aims, factional collusion could not be restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang, every successor was a castrated man. On first entering court they tended to be clever, nimble, and adept at holding royal favor; once they rose to power, their cliques and entanglements proved impossible to curb.

sentences.zh: 東漢以宦者亡，唐又甚焉。

translations.literal: The Eastern Han perished through eunuchs; the Tang suffered even worse.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Han dynasty fell victim to its eunuchs; the Tang suffered worse still.

sentences.zh: 世儒論宦者之害，如毒藥猛虎之不可拯也。

translations.literal: Scholars of the age discussed the harm of eunuchs as something that could not be remedied, like poison or fierce tigers.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary literati spoke of the damage done by eunuchs as an evil no more remediable than poison or a ravening tiger.

sentences.zh: 金法置近侍局，嘗與政事，而宦者少與焉。

translations.literal: Jin law established the Bureau of Personal Attendants, which at times participated in government affairs, but eunuchs had little part therein.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin law the Bureau of Personal Attendants was set up and sometimes took part in state affairs, yet eunuchs figured in that role only rarely.

sentences.zh: 惟海陵時有梁珫，章宗時有梁道、李新喜幹政，二君為所誤多矣。

translations.literal: Only under Emperor Hailing was there Liang Chong, and under Emperor Zhangzong there were Liang Dao and Li Xinxi interfering in government—both rulers were misled by them in many ways.
translations.idiomatic: Only in Hailing's reign did Liang Chong wield power; only under Zhangzong did Liang Dao and Li Xinxi meddle in government—and both emperors were led astray by them again and again.

sentences.zh: 世傳梁道勸章宗納李妃後宮，金史不載梁道始末，弗得而論次之。

translations.literal: It is transmitted that Liang Dao urged Zhangzong to take Consort Li into the rear palace; the Jin History does not record Liang Dao's origins and end, so he cannot be evaluated in order.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition holds that Liang Dao urged Zhangzong to install Consort Li in the inner palace, but the Jin History does not record his career from beginning to end, so he cannot be assessed here in due order.

sentences.zh: 惟宋珪、潘守恆頗能諷諫宣、哀，時有裨益，蓋傭之佼佼、鐵之錚錚者也。

translations.literal: Only Song Gui and Pan Shouheng were quite able to offer indirect remonstrance to Emperors Xuan and Ai, and at times were of benefit—they were outstanding among hired men and ringing among iron.
translations.idiomatic: Only Song Gui and Pan Shouheng were able to offer pointed, indirect remonstrance to Emperors Xuan and Ai and at times did real good—outstanding among hirelings, ringing true as tempered iron.

sentences.zh: 作《宦者傳》。

translations.literal: [The history] composes the "Biographies of Eunuchs."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the compilation of the Biographies of Eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 梁珫，本大抃家奴，隨元妃入宮，以閹豎事海陵。

translations.literal: Liang Chong was originally a household slave of the Dabian family; he followed the primary consort into the palace and served Emperor Hailing as a castrated attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chong had begun as a slave in the Dabian household. He entered the palace with the primary consort and, as a castrated attendant, served Emperor Hailing.

sentences.zh: 珫性便佞，善迎合，特見寵信，舊制，宦者惟掌掖廷宮闈之事。

translations.literal: Chong was artful and fawning, skilled at ingratiation, and received special favor and trust. By old regulation, eunuchs managed only the inner palace and women's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was smooth and obsequious, expert at currying favor, and won exceptional trust. Under the old rules eunuchs handled only the inner palace and women's quarters.

sentences.zh: 天德三年，始以王光道為內藏庫使，衛愈、梁安仁皆以宦官領內藏。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiande, Wang Guangdao was first made Director of the Inner Treasury; Wei Yu and Liang Anren also, as eunuchs, headed the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiande (1151), Wang Guangdao became the first Director of the Inner Treasury; Wei Yu and Liang Anren likewise took charge of the inner treasury as eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 海陵謂光道等曰：「人言宦者不可用，朕以為不然。

translations.literal: Hailing said to Guangdao and the others: "People say eunuchs cannot be used; I do not think so.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing told Guangdao and the others, "People say eunuchs are useless. I disagree.

sentences.zh: 後唐莊宗委張承業以軍，竟立大功，此中豈無人乎。

translations.literal: Later Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong entrusted Zhang Chengye with the army and he in the end achieved great merit—is there truly no such man among these?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang entrusted Zhang Chengye with his armies, and Zhang won great distinction—surely capable men can be found among you as well.

sentences.zh: 卿等宜悉此意。

translations.literal: You all should fully grasp this intent.
translations.idiomatic: Take this to heart.

sentences.zh: 帑藏之物皆出民力，費十致一，當糾察奸弊，犯者必罰無赦。

translations.literal: Treasury goods all come from the people's strength; ten parts spent yield one part received—you must investigate malfeasance, and offenders must be punished without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Everything in the treasury comes from the people's labor—ten parts spent may yield only one part stored. Root out fraud and abuse; offenders must be punished without mercy.

sentences.zh: 」宦者始與政事，而珫委任尤甚，累官近侍局使。

translations.literal: " Eunuchs began to participate in government affairs, and Chong's commission was especially heavy; he rose through offices to become Director of the Bureau of Personal Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on eunuchs took part in government, and Chong's authority was greater than any other's; he rose step by step to head the Bureau of Personal Attendants.

sentences.zh: 及營建南京宮室，海陵數數使珫往視工役。

translations.literal: When the Southern Capital palace was being built, Hailing repeatedly sent Chong to inspect the labor.
translations.idiomatic: While the Southern Capital palace was under construction, Hailing sent Chong again and again to inspect the work.

sentences.zh: 是時，一殿之費已不可勝計，珫或言其未善，即盡撒去。

translations.literal: At that time the cost of a single hall was already beyond counting; if Chong sometimes said it was not good enough, it was immediately torn down entirely.
translations.idiomatic: By then a single hall's cost was beyond reckoning; if Chong said the work was not good enough, the whole structure was torn down at once.

sentences.zh: 雖丞相張浩亦曲意事之，與之均禮。

translations.literal: Even Chancellor Zhang Hao bent his will to serve him and treated him as an equal in ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Even Chancellor Zhang Hao deferred to him and accorded him equal ceremonial standing.

sentences.zh: 海陵欲伐宋，珫因極言宋劉貴妃絕色傾國。

translations.literal: When Hailing wished to attack Song, Chong therefore spoke at length of how Song's Honored Consort Liu was of peerless beauty that could overturn a state.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing planned to attack the Song, Chong dwelt at length on the peerless beauty of the Song Honored Consort Liu, beauty said to be enough to topple a realm.

sentences.zh: 海陵大喜，及南征將行，命縣君高師姑兒貯衾褥之新潔者俟得劉貴妃用之。

translations.literal: Hailing was greatly pleased; when the southern campaign was about to depart, he ordered the county lady Gao Shigu'er to store fresh, clean bedding and quilts to await use when Honored Consort Liu was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was delighted. As the southern campaign was about to set out, he ordered the county lady Gao Shigu'er to keep fresh bedding ready for the day he might take Honored Consort Liu.

sentences.zh: 議者言珫與宋通謀，勸帝伐宋，征天下兵以疲弊中國。

translations.literal: Critics said Chong conspired with Song, urged the emperor to attack Song, and mobilized troops empire-wide to exhaust and weaken China.
translations.idiomatic: Some charged that Chong was in league with the Song—that he had urged the emperor to invade the south and levy troops empire-wide in order to wear down the Jin state.

sentences.zh: 海陵至和州，聞珫與宋人交通有狀，謂珫曰：「聞汝與宋國交通，傳泄事情。

translations.literal: When Hailing reached Hezhou, he heard there was evidence of Chong's dealings with Song men, and said to Chong: "I hear you have dealings with the Song state and leak affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing reached Hezhou he learned there was proof of Chong's traffic with the Song. He told Chong, "I hear you have been dealing with the Song and leaking state business.

sentences.zh: 汝本奴隸，朕拔擢至此，乃敢爾耶。

translations.literal: You were originally a slave; I raised and promoted you to this position—how dare you act thus?
translations.idiomatic: You were a slave; I raised you to this height—how dare you do such a thing?

sentences.zh: 若至江南詢得實跡，殺汝亦未晚也。

translations.literal: If upon reaching Jiangnan inquiry obtains solid proof, killing you will not yet be too late.
translations.idiomatic: If we reach the south and inquiry confirms it, your execution will not be too late.

sentences.zh: 」又謂校書郎田與信曰：「爾面目亦可疑，必與珫同謀者。

translations.literal: " He also said to the collator Tian Yuxin: "Your face is also suspicious—you must be Chong's co-conspirator.
translations.idiomatic: " He also told the collator Tian Yuxin, "Your face looks suspicious too—you must be Chong's accomplice.

sentences.zh: 」皆命執於軍中。

translations.literal: " Both were ordered seized in the army.
translations.idiomatic: " Both were ordered taken into military custody.

sentences.zh: 海陵遇弑，珫、與信皆為亂軍所殺。

translations.literal: When Hailing met assassination, Chong and Yuxin were both killed by the mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing was assassinated, Chong and Yuxin were both killed by the mutinous soldiers.

sentences.zh: 宋珪，本名乞奴，燕人也。

translations.literal: Song Gui, original name Qinu, was a man of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Song Gui, whose original name was Qinu, came from the Yan region.

sentences.zh: 為內侍殿頭。

translations.literal: He served as head of the inner attendants' hall.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of head attendant in the inner service.

sentences.zh: 宣宗嘗以元夕欲觀燈戲，命乞奴監作，乞奴誶語雲：「社稷棄之中都，南京作燈戲有何看耶。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan once on the Lantern Festival wished to watch lantern plays and ordered Qinu to supervise their production; Qinu cursed, saying: "The altars and grain abandoned at Zhongdu—what is there to see in lantern plays at the Southern Capital?
translations.idiomatic: On one Lantern Festival Emperor Xuan wished to watch lantern plays and put Qinu in charge of staging them. Qinu swore aloud: "The realm was abandoned at Zhongdu—what is there to watch in lantern plays at the Southern Capital?

sentences.zh: 」宣宗微聞之，杖之二十，既而悔之，有旨宣諭。

translations.literal: " Xuan faintly heard of it, had him beaten twenty strokes, then regretted it and issued an edict of reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan caught wind of it and had him beaten twenty strokes, then regretted it and sent an edict to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 哀宗放鷂後苑，鷂逸去，敕近侍追訪之，市中一農民臂此鷂，近侍不敢言宮中所逸者，百方索之，農民不與，與之物直，僅乃得。

translations.literal: Emperor Ai released a goshawk in the rear garden; the goshawk escaped. He ordered personal attendants to pursue and seek it. In the market a farmer had this goshawk on his arm; the attendants dared not say it was the palace's escaped bird and sought it by every means; the farmer would not give it up until they paid its price in goods, and only then obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai released a goshawk in the rear garden and it escaped. He ordered his personal attendants to recover it. In the market a farmer was carrying the bird on his arm; the attendants did not dare say it was the palace falcon and tried every means to get it back. The farmer refused until they paid him its value in goods, and only then did they secure it.

sentences.zh: 事聞，哀宗欲送其人於有司，乞奴從旁諫曰：「貴畜賤人，豈可宣示四方。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Ai wished to hand the man over to the authorities; Qinu remonstrated from the side, saying: "To value beasts and slight men—how can this be displayed to the four quarters?
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported, Ai wanted to hand the farmer over to the authorities. Qinu remonstrated beside him: "To prize a bird and slight a man—how can we display that to the empire?

sentences.zh: 」哀宗惡其大訐，又仗之，尋亦悔，賜物慰遣之。

translations.literal: " Ai disliked his bold remonstrance and beat him again; soon he also regretted it and bestowed goods to comfort and dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: " Ai took offense at his bluntness and had him beaten again, but soon regretted it and sent gifts to console him.

sentences.zh: 及哀宗至歸德，馬軍元帥蒲察官奴為變，殺左丞李蹊、參政石盞女魯歡以下從官三百餘人。

translations.literal: When Ai reached Guide, the cavalry commander Pucha Guannu mutinied and killed the Left Vice Chancellor Li Xi, the Councilor Shizhan Nülühuan, and more than three hundred attending officials below them.
translations.idiomatic: When Ai reached Guide, the cavalry commander Pucha Guannu rose in mutiny and killed the Left Vice Chancellor Li Xi, the Councilor Shizhan Nülühuan, and more than three hundred officials in their train.

sentences.zh: 倉皇之際，哀宗不得已，以官奴權參知政事，既為所制，含恨欲誅之未能也。

translations.literal: In the emergency Ai had no choice but to make Guannu acting Associate Director of the Secretariat; once controlled by him, he harbored resentment and wished to execute him but could not.
translations.idiomatic: In the crisis Ai had no choice but to appoint Guannu acting Associate Director of the Secretariat. Once under his control, Ai nursed hatred and wished to kill him but could not.

sentences.zh: 及官奴往亳州，珪陰與奉禦吾古孫愛實、納蘭忔答，護衛女奚烈完出、范陳僧、王山兒等謀誅之。

translations.literal: When Guannu went to Bozhou, Gui secretly with the palace attendant Wugusun Aishi, Nalan Yida, the guardswoman Xilie Wanchu, Fan Chenseng, Wang Shan'er, and others plotted to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: When Guannu went to Bozhou, Gui secretly joined the palace attendant Wugusun Aishi, Nalan Yida, the guardswoman Xilie Wanchu, Fan Chenseng, Wang Shan'er, and others in a plot to kill him.

sentences.zh: 官奴自亳還，哀宗禦臨漪亭，召參政張天綱及官奴議事。

translations.literal: When Guannu returned from Bo, Ai held court at the Yiting Pavilion and summoned the Councilor Zhang Tiangang and Guannu to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Guannu returned from Bo, Ai held audience at the Yiting Pavilion and summoned Councilor Zhang Tiangang and Guannu to discuss affairs.

sentences.zh: 官奴入見，珪等即從旁殺之，及其党阿裏合、白進、習顯。

translations.literal: When Guannu entered for audience, Gui and the others immediately killed him from the side, along with his partisans Alihe, Bai Jin, and Xi Xian.
translations.idiomatic: As Guannu entered for audience, Gui and the others struck him down on the spot, along with his partisans Alihe, Bai Jin, and Xi Xian.

sentences.zh: 及蔡城破，哀宗自縊于幽蘭軒，珪與完顏斜烈、焦春和等皆從死。

translations.literal: When Caicheng fell, Ai hanged himself in the Youlan Pavilion; Gui, Wanyan Xielie, Jiao Chunhe, and others all followed him in death.
translations.idiomatic: When Caicheng fell, Ai hanged himself in the Youlan Pavilion; Gui, Wanyan Xielie, Jiao Chunhe, and others died with him.

sentences.zh: 潘守恆

translations.literal: Pan Shouheng
translations.idiomatic: Pan Shouheng

sentences.zh: 有潘守恆者亦內侍也，素稱知書，南遷後規益甚多。

translations.literal: There was also Pan Shouheng, likewise an inner attendant, long reputed learned; after the southward move his admonitions and benefits were many.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Pan Shouheng, another inner attendant, long known as a man of learning; after the court moved south his counsel proved of great benefit.

sentences.zh: 及哀宗自蒲城走歸德，道次民家，守恆進櫛，曰：「願陛下還宮之日無忘此草廬中，更加儉素，以濟大業。

translations.literal: When Ai fled from Pucheng to Guide, stopping at a commoner's house along the way, Shouheng presented a comb and said: "May Your Majesty on the day of returning to the palace not forget this thatched hut, and further practice frugality and simplicity to accomplish the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: When Ai fled from Pucheng toward Guide and lodged at a commoner's house along the way, Shouheng brought him a comb and said, "When Your Majesty returns to the palace, may you not forget this thatched dwelling—practice still greater frugality to carry through the great cause.

sentences.zh: 」上聞其言，淒惋咨嗟久之。

translations.literal: " On hearing his words, the emperor mourned and sighed in consultation for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor heard him and grieved aloud, sighing for a long while.

sentences.zh: 太史公敘九流，述《日者》、《龜策》、《扁鵲倉公列傳》。

translations.literal: Grand Historian Sima narrated the Nine Schools and composed the "Biographies of Day-Selectors," "Tortoise and Yarrow," and "Bian Que and the Lord of Cang."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Historian Sima surveyed the Nine Schools and wrote the biographies of day-selectors, tortoise-and-yarrow diviners, and the physicians Bian Que and the Lord of Cang.

sentences.zh: 劉歆校中秘書，以術數、方伎載之《七略》。

translations.literal: Liu Xin collated the palace secretariat books and placed numerology and technical arts in the Seven Summaries.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin collated the imperial library and entered numerology and technical arts in his Seven Summaries.

sentences.zh: 後世史官作《方伎傳》，蓋祖其意焉。

translations.literal: Later dynasties' historians composed "Biographies of Technical Arts," broadly following his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Later historians wrote Biographies of Technical Arts in much the same spirit.

sentences.zh: 或曰《素問》、《內經》言天道消長、氣運贏縮，假醫術，托岐黃，以傳其秘奧耳。

translations.literal: Some say the Plain Questions and Inner Canon speak of heaven's way waxing and waning and qi's fortune winning and losing, borrowing medicine and entrusting it to Qi and Huang to transmit their secret profundities.
translations.idiomatic: Some hold that the Plain Questions and Inner Canon really treat the waxing and waning of heaven's way and the ebb and flow of cosmic qi—that they merely borrow the language of medicine and the names of Qi Bo and the Yellow Emperor to convey deeper mysteries.

sentences.zh: 秦人至以《周易》列之卜筮，斯豈易言哉！

translations.literal: Qin men even placed the Book of Changes among divination by stalk and tortoise—this is surely not easily spoken of!
translations.idiomatic: The Qin even classed the Book of Changes under divination—such matters are not lightly judged!

sentences.zh: 第古之為術，以吉凶導人而為善，後世術者，或以休咎導人為不善，古之為醫，以活人為功，後世醫者，或因以為利而誤殺人。

translations.literal: Only in antiquity those who practiced arts used fortune and misfortune to guide people toward good; later practitioners sometimes used omens to guide people toward evil. In antiquity physicians took saving lives as merit; later physicians sometimes used it for profit and by mistake killed people.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity practitioners used omens of fortune and misfortune to steer people toward the good; later ones sometimes used such signs to lead them astray. Ancient physicians took saving lives as their merit; later ones sometimes turned medicine to profit and killed patients by mistake.

sentences.zh: 故為政於天下，雖方伎之事，亦必慎其所職掌，而務旌別其賢否焉。

translations.literal: Therefore in governing the realm, even in technical arts one must be careful in what offices are charged, and strive to distinguish the worthy from the unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever governs the realm must therefore be careful even in technical arts—watch closely what offices they hold and clearly mark the worthy apart from the unworthy.

sentences.zh: 金世，如武禎、武亢之信而不誣，劉完素、張元素之治療通變，學其術者皆師尊之，不可不記雲。

translations.literal: In the Jin age, such as Wu Zhen and Wu Kang—faithful and not deceitful; Liu Wansu and Zhang Yuansu—treatment adaptable to change: those who studied their arts all honored them as teachers; they cannot go unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jin, men such as Wu Zhen and Wu Kang proved trustworthy and free of deceit; Liu Wansu and Zhang Yuansu mastered treatment that adapted to changing conditions—all who studied their arts revered them as teachers, and they must be recorded.

sentences.zh: 劉完素

translations.literal: Liu Wansu
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wansu

sentences.zh: 劉完素，字守真，河間人。

translations.literal: Liu Wansu, style name Shouzhen, was a man of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wansu, whose style was Shouzhen, came from Hejian.

sentences.zh: 嘗遇異人陳先生，以酒飲守真，大醉，及寤洞達醫術，若有授之者。

translations.literal: He once met the extraordinary man Master Chen, who made Shouzhen drink wine until greatly drunk; when he awoke he thoroughly penetrated medical arts, as if someone had imparted them.
translations.idiomatic: He once met a remarkable man, Master Chen, who plied Shouzhen with wine until he was deeply drunk; when he woke he had mastered medicine as though it had been handed to him whole.

sentences.zh: 乃撰《運氣要旨論》、《精要宣明論》，慮庸醫或出妄說，又著《素問玄機原病式》，特舉二百八十八字，注二萬餘言。

translations.literal: He then composed Essentials of Qi Cycles and Clarified Essentials of the Essential, fearing mediocre physicians might put forth reckless doctrines; he also wrote Patterns of Original Disease from the Plain Questions' Mysteries, specially citing two hundred eighty-eight characters and annotating them with more than twenty thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Essentials of Qi Cycles and Clarified Essentials of the Essential, fearing that mediocre physicians might spread reckless theories. He also wrote Patterns of Original Disease from the Plain Questions' Mysteries, taking two hundred eighty-eight key characters from the canon and annotating them in more than twenty thousand words.

sentences.zh: 然好用涼劑，以降心火、益腎水為主。

translations.literal: Yet he was fond of using cooling drugs, chiefly to lower heart fire and supplement kidney water.
translations.idiomatic: He favored cooling medicines, chiefly to reduce heart fire and strengthen kidney water.

sentences.zh: 自號「通元處士」雲。

translations.literal: He styled himself "Retired Scholar Who Penetrates the Origin."
translations.idiomatic: He took for himself the sobriquet "Retired Scholar Who Penetrates the Origin."

sentences.zh: 張從正

translations.literal: Zhang Congzheng
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Congzheng

sentences.zh: 張從正，字子和，睢州考城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Congzheng, style name Zihe, was a man of Kaocheng in Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Congzheng, whose style was Zihe, came from Kaocheng in Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 精於醫，貫穿《難》、《素》之學，其法宗劉守真，用藥多寒涼，然起疾救死多取效。

translations.literal: He was expert in medicine and penetrated the learning of the Difficult Issues and Plain Questions; his method followed Liu Shouzhen, using mostly cold and cool drugs, yet in raising illness and saving the dying he often achieved effect.
translations.idiomatic: He was a master physician who had mastered the Difficult Issues and Plain Questions. His method followed Liu Shouzhen and relied heavily on cold and cooling drugs, yet he often succeeded in reviving the gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 古醫書有《汗下吐法》，亦有不當汗者汗之則死，不當下者下之則死，不當吐者吐之則死，各有經絡脈理，世傳黃帝、岐伯所為書也。

translations.literal: Ancient medical books have the methods of sweating, purging, and vomiting; there are also cases where those who should not be sweated die if sweated, those who should not be purged die if purged, those who should not be vomited die if vomited—each has its channels, collaterals, and pulse principles; the world transmits them as books made by the Yellow Emperor and Qi Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient medical texts teach the methods of sweating, purging, and vomiting—but to sweat when one should not, purge when one should not, or vomit when one should not is to kill the patient. Each case has its proper channels, collaterals, and pulse logic. Tradition attributes these books to the Yellow Emperor and Qi Bo.

sentences.zh: 從正用之最精，號「張子和汗下吐法」。

translations.literal: Congzheng used them with greatest refinement and was styled "Master Zhang Zihe's Methods of Sweating, Purging, and Vomiting."
translations.idiomatic: Congzheng wielded these methods with supreme skill and was known as "Master Zhang Zihe's sweating, purging, and vomiting therapy."

sentences.zh: 妄庸淺術習其方劑，不知察脈原病，往往殺人，此庸醫所以失其傳之過也。

translations.literal: Reckless mediocre shallow practitioners studied his formulas without knowing how to examine pulses and trace original disease, and often killed people—this is the fault by which mediocre physicians lost the transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Mediocre practitioners who copied his formulas without learning to read the pulse or trace the root of disease often killed their patients—that is how the art was betrayed by poor physicians.

sentences.zh: 其所著有「六門、二法」之目，存於世雲。

translations.literal: His writings include the categories "Six Gates" and "Two Methods," preserved in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His writings, including the categories "Six Gates" and "Two Methods," survive to this day.

sentences.zh: 李慶嗣

translations.literal: Li Qingsi
translations.idiomatic: Li Qingsi

sentences.zh: 李慶嗣，洺人。

translations.literal: Li Qingsi was a man of Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qingsi came from Mo.

sentences.zh: 少舉進士不第，棄而學醫，讀《素問》諸書，洞曉其義。

translations.literal: In youth he attempted the jinshi examination without success, abandoned it and studied medicine, read the Plain Questions and related books, and thoroughly understood their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he failed the jinshi examination, turned to medicine, studied the Plain Questions and related texts, and mastered their meaning.

sentences.zh: 天德間，歲大疫，廣平尤甚，貧者往往闔門臥病。

translations.literal: During the Tiande era, in a year of great pestilence, Guangping suffered especially; the poor often had whole households bedridden with illness.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiande era a great epidemic struck; Guangping was hit hardest, and poor families often saw every member of the household fall ill.

sentences.zh: 廣嗣攜藥與米分遺之，全活者眾。

translations.literal: Qingsi carried medicine and rice to distribute to them; many were wholly saved.
translations.idiomatic: Qingsi went about distributing medicine and rice; he saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 慶嗣年八十餘，無疾而終。

translations.literal: Qingsi lived more than eighty years and ended without illness.
translations.idiomatic: Qingsi lived past eighty and died without illness.

sentences.zh: 所著《傷寒纂類》四卷、《改證活人書》三卷、《傷寒論》三卷、《針經》一卷，傳於世。

translations.literal: His works Collected Categories of Cold Damage in four scrolls, Revised Evidence for the Book that Saves Lives in three scrolls, Treatise on Cold Damage in three scrolls, and Classic of Acupuncture in one scroll, are transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His works—Collected Categories of Cold Damage (four scrolls), Revised Evidence for the Book that Saves Lives (three scrolls), Treatise on Cold Damage (three scrolls), and Classic of Acupuncture (one scroll)—circulate to this day.

sentences.zh: 紀天錫

translations.literal: Ji Tianxi
translations.idiomatic: Ji Tianxi

sentences.zh: 紀天錫，字齊卿，泰安人。

translations.literal: Ji Tianxi, style name Qiqing, was a man of Tai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Tianxi, whose style was Qiqing, came from Tai'an.

sentences.zh: 早棄進士業，學醫，精於其技，遂以醫名世。

translations.literal: He early abandoned the jinshi career, studied medicine, became expert in the art, and thereby made his name in the world through medicine.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned the jinshi path early, took up medicine, mastered the art, and won fame throughout the realm as a physician.

sentences.zh: 集注《難經》五卷，大定十五年上其書，授醫學博士。

translations.literal: He compiled a commentary on the Difficult Classic in five scrolls; in the fifteenth year of Dading he presented his book and was appointed Doctor of Medicine.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled a five-scroll commentary on the Difficult Classic. In the fifteenth year of Dading (1155) he presented it to the throne and was appointed Doctor of Medicine.

sentences.zh: 張元素

translations.literal: Zhang Yuansu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuansu

sentences.zh: 張元素，字潔古，易州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuansu, style name Jiegu, was a man of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuansu, whose style was Jiegu, came from Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 八歲試童子舉。

translations.literal: At eight he attempted the childhood examination.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he sat for the childhood examination.

sentences.zh: 二十七試經義進士，犯廟諱下第。

translations.literal: At twenty-seven he attempted the jinshi in classical exegesis and failed for violating taboo on the imperial temple name.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-seven he took the jinshi examination in classical exegesis but failed because his composition violated the imperial temple taboo.

sentences.zh: 乃去學醫，無所知名，夜夢有人用大斧長鑿鑿心開竅，納書數卷於其中，自是洞徹其術。

translations.literal: He then left to study medicine without any renown; one night he dreamed someone used a great axe and long chisel to bore open his heart, placed several scrolls of books within, and from then thoroughly penetrated the art.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned to medicine without yet making a name. One night he dreamed that a man opened his chest with a great axe and long chisel, placed several scrolls inside, and from that moment he mastered the art completely.

sentences.zh: 河間劉完素病傷寒八日，頭痛脈緊，嘔逆不食，不和所為。

translations.literal: Liu Wansu of Hejian fell ill with cold damage for eight days, with headache, tight pulse, vomiting and retching, and inability to eat—he did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wansu of Hejian had been ill with cold damage for eight days—headache, a tight pulse, vomiting, and inability to eat—and did not know what course to take.

sentences.zh: 元素往候，完素面壁不顧，元素曰：「何見待之卑如此哉。

translations.literal: Yuansu went to visit; Wansu faced the wall and paid no attention. Yuansu said: "Why do you treat me with such low regard?
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu went to call on him, but Wansu turned to the wall and ignored him. Yuansu said, "Why do you treat me with such contempt?

sentences.zh: 」既為診脈，謂之曰脈病云云，曰：「然。

translations.literal: " Having examined his pulse, he told him the pulse and disease thus and so; [Wansu] said: "So it is.
translations.idiomatic: " After taking his pulse he described the condition in detail. Wansu said, "Exactly so.

sentences.zh: 」「初服某藥，用某味乎？

translations.literal: " "Did you at first take such-and-such medicine, using such-and-such ingredient?
translations.idiomatic: " "Did you first take such-and-such medicine, using such-and-such ingredient?

translations.literal: " [Wansu] said: "So it is.
translations.idiomatic: " "Yes," he said.

sentences.zh: 」元素曰：「子誤矣。

translations.literal: " Yuansu said: "You are mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuansu said, "You are in error.

sentences.zh: 某味性寒，下降走太陰，陽亡汗不能出。

translations.literal: Such-and-such ingredient is cold in nature, descends and travels the greater yin; yang is lost and sweat cannot emerge.
translations.idiomatic: That ingredient is cold in nature; it drives downward along the greater yin channel, yang is depleted, and sweat cannot break through.

sentences.zh: 今脈如此，當服某藥則效矣。

translations.literal: Now with the pulse like this, you should take such-and-such medicine and it will be effective.
translations.idiomatic: With the pulse as it is now, you should take such-and-such medicine and you will recover.

sentences.zh: 」完素大服，如其言遂愈，元素自此顯名。

translations.literal: " Wansu was greatly convinced; following his words he then recovered, and Yuansu from then became famous.
translations.idiomatic: " Wansu was deeply impressed. He followed the prescription and recovered; from that day Yuansu's name spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 平素治病不用古方，其說曰：「運氣不齊，古今異軌，古方新病不相能也。

translations.literal: In ordinary times in treating disease he did not use ancient formulas; his doctrine said: "Qi cycles are not uniform; ancient and modern follow different tracks—ancient formulas and new diseases cannot suit each other.
translations.idiomatic: In practice he did not rely on ancient formulas. His teaching ran: "Qi cycles are never uniform; ancient and modern times follow different courses—ancient formulas cannot meet new diseases.

sentences.zh: 」自為家法雲。

translations.literal: " He made this his own school method.
translations.idiomatic: " This became his own school of practice.

sentences.zh: 馬貴中

translations.literal: Ma Guizhong
translations.idiomatic: Ma Guizhong

sentences.zh: 馬貴中，天德中，為司天提點。

translations.literal: Ma Guizhong, during Tiande, served as Supervisor of the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiande era Ma Guizhong served as Supervisor of the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 與校書郎高守元奏天象災異忤旨，海陵皆杖之，黜貴中為大同府判官。

translations.literal: With the collator Gao Shouyuan he memorialized on celestial phenomena and disasters and omens, offending the emperor's intent; Hailing had them both beaten with the staff and demoted Guizhong to be judge of Datong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He and the collator Gao Shouyuan memorialized on celestial omens and disasters in a manner that displeased the throne. Hailing had them both beaten and demoted Guizhong to judge of Datong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷司天監。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Director of the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was promoted to Director of the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 正隆三年三月辛酉朔，日當食。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenglong, third month, first day xinyou, the sun was due to be eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenglong (1158), on the first day of the third month (a xinyou day), a solar eclipse was expected.

sentences.zh: 是日，候之不食，海陵謂貴中曰：「自今凡遇日食皆面奏，不須頒示內外。」

translations.literal: That day they awaited it but there was no eclipse. Hailing said to Guizhong: "From now on, whenever there is a solar eclipse, report it in person at court; there is no need to promulgate it within and without."
translations.idiomatic: That day they waited, but the sun was not eclipsed. Hailing told Guizhong, "From now on, report every eclipse to me in person at court—do not issue proclamations inside and outside the palace."

sentences.zh: 海陵伐宋，問曰：「朕欲自將伐宋，天道何如？

translations.literal: When Hailing attacked Song he asked: "I wish to command the attack on Song in person—how stands heaven's way?
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing prepared to attack the Song, he asked, "I intend to lead the campaign against the Song in person—what do the heavens indicate?

sentences.zh: 」貴中對曰：「去年十月甲戌，熒惑順入太微，至屏星，留、退、西出。

translations.literal: " Guizhong replied: "Last year, tenth month, day jiaxu, Mars moving direct entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure, reached the Screen Star, stayed, retreated, and exited west.
translations.idiomatic: " Guizhong answered, "Last year, in the tenth month on a jiaxu day, Mars moved direct into the Supreme Palace Enclosure, reached the Screen Star, lingered, retreated, and departed westward."

sentences.zh: 《占書》，熒惑常以十月入太微庭，受制出伺無道之國。

translations.literal: Divination books say Mars often enters the Supreme Palace courtyard in the tenth month, receives constraint, and goes out to watch states without the Way.
translations.idiomatic: According to the books of divination, Mars regularly enters the Supreme Palace courtyard in the tenth month, is constrained, and then goes forth to observe states that have lost the Way.

sentences.zh: 十二月，太白晝見經天，占為兵喪、為不臣、為更主，又主有兵兵罷、無兵兵起。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Venus was seen in daytime crossing heaven—its omens are army mourning, disloyal subjects, and change of ruler; it also signifies that if there is war, war ends; if there is no war, war arises.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Venus appeared in daylight and crossed the sky—omens of war and mourning, of disloyal ministers, and of a change of ruler; it also means that if war is underway it will end, and if there is no war war will break out.

sentences.zh: 」鎮戎軍地震大風，海陵以問，貴中對曰：「伏陰逼陽，所以震也。

translations.literal: " At Zhenrong Army there was an earthquake and great wind. Hailing asked; Guizhong replied: "Hidden yin pressing yang—that is why it quakes.
translations.idiomatic: " At Zhenrong Army there was an earthquake and a great wind. Hailing inquired, and Guizhong answered, "Yin forces pent up are pressing yang—that is why the earth quakes."

sentences.zh: 」又問曰：「當震，大風何也？

translations.literal: " He asked again: "When it should quake, why is there great wind?
translations.idiomatic: " He asked again, "If an earthquake is due, why is there a great wind?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「土失其性則地震，風為號令，人君命令嚴急，則有烈風及物之災。

translations.literal: " He replied: "When earth loses its nature there is earthquake; wind is command—when the ruler's commands are severe and urgent, there are fierce winds and disasters upon things.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "When earth loses its proper nature the ground quakes. Wind stands for command—when the ruler's orders are harsh and urgent, fierce winds and disasters upon things follow."

sentences.zh: 」六年二月甲辰朔，日有暈珥戴背，海陵問：「近日天道何如？

translations.literal: " In the sixth year, second month, first day jiachen, the sun had halo, ear-rings, canopy, and back-arc. Hailing asked: "How has heaven's way been recently?
translations.idiomatic: " In the sixth year, on the first day of the second month (a jiachen day), the sun showed a halo, ear-rings, a canopy, and a back-arc. Hailing asked, "What have the heavens shown of late?"

sentences.zh: 」貴中對曰：「前年八月二十九日，太白入太微右掖門，九月二日，至端門，九日，至左掖門出，並曆左右執法。

translations.literal: " Guizhong replied: "The year before last, eighth month, twenty-ninth day, Venus entered the Supreme Palace right side gate; ninth month, second day, reached the central gate; ninth day, reached the left side gate and exited—all passing the left and right law enforcers.
translations.idiomatic: " Guizhong answered, "Two years ago, on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth month, Venus entered the right side gate of the Supreme Palace Enclosure; on the second day of the ninth month it reached the central gate; on the ninth it passed out through the left side gate—each time crossing the left and right law-enforcer stars."

sentences.zh: 太微為天子南宮，太白兵將之象，其占，兵入天子之廷。

translations.literal: The Supreme Palace is the Son of Heaven's southern palace; Venus is the image of armies and generals—its omen: armies enter the Son of Heaven's court.
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme Palace Enclosure is the Son of Heaven's southern palace; Venus is the sign of armies and generals—its omen is that armed forces enter the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 」海陵曰：「今將征伐而兵將出入太微，正其事也。

translations.literal: " Hailing said: "Now about to campaign while armies and generals pass in and out of the Supreme Palace—that fits the affair.
translations.idiomatic: " Hailing said, "We are about to campaign, and armies and generals are passing in and out of the Supreme Palace—that suits the occasion exactly."

sentences.zh: 」貴中又曰；

translations.literal: " Guizhong also said:
translations.idiomatic: " Guizhong added:

sentences.zh: 「當端門而出，其占為受制，曆左右執法為受事，此當有出使者，或為兵，或為賊。

translations.literal: "Exiting at the central gate—its omen is receiving constraint; passing the left and right law enforcers is receiving assignments—there should be envoys going out, whether as armies or as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: "When it exits at the central gate the omen is one of constraint; passing the left and right law-enforcer stars means receiving assignments—envoys will go forth, whether as armies or as bandits."

sentences.zh: 」海陵曰：「兵興之際，小盜固不能無也。

translations.literal: " Hailing said: "In times when armies rise, small thieves naturally cannot be absent.
translations.idiomatic: " Hailing said, "When armies are on the march, petty bandits are bound to appear."

sentences.zh: 」及被害於揚州，貴中之言皆驗。

translations.literal: " When he was killed at Yangzhou, all Guizhong's words were verified.
translations.idiomatic: " When Hailing was killed at Yangzhou, every one of Guizhong's predictions was borne out.

sentences.zh: 大定八年，世宗擊球于常武殿，貴中上疏諫曰：「陛下為天下主，守宗廟社稷之重，圍獵擊球皆危事也。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dading, Shizong played ball at the Changwu Hall. Guizhong submitted a memorial remonstrating: "Your Majesty is master of the realm, bearing the weight of ancestral temples and altars—hunting and ball games are all dangerous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dading (1168), Shizong played cuju at the Changwu Hall. Guizhong submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "Your Majesty is sovereign of the realm and bears the weight of the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain—hunting and ball games are perilous pursuits."

sentences.zh: 前日皇太子墜馬，可以為戒，臣願一切罷之。

translations.literal: The other day the crown prince fell from a horse—that can serve as a warning; your servant begs that all these be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince fell from his horse the other day—that should be warning enough. I beg Your Majesty to abandon such pastimes altogether."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「祖宗以武定天下，豈以承平遽忘之邪。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Our ancestors by arms settled the realm—how, because of peace, suddenly forget it?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied, "Our ancestors settled the realm by force of arms—how could we forget that simply because we now enjoy peace?

sentences.zh: 皇統嘗罷此事，當時之人皆以為非，朕所親見，故示天下以習武耳。」

translations.literal: During Huangtong this matter was abolished; people of that time all thought it wrong. I saw it personally, and therefore show the realm martial training."
translations.idiomatic: In the Huangtong era this practice was abolished, and everyone at the time thought that a mistake. I saw it with my own eyes, which is why I mean to show the realm that we still train in arms."

sentences.zh: 十年十一月，皇太子生日，世宗宴百官於東宮。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, eleventh month, on the crown prince's birthday, Shizong feasted the hundred officials at the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, eleventh month, on the crown prince's birthday, Shizong gave a feast for the officials at the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 上飲歡甚，貴中被酒，前跪欲言事，錯亂失次，上不之罪，但令扶出。

translations.literal: The emperor drank very merrily; Guizhong was drunk, knelt forward wishing to speak on affairs, confused and out of order; the emperor did not punish him, only had him assisted out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drank heartily. Guizhong, drunk, knelt forward to speak on some matter but stumbled over his words. The emperor did not punish him—he merely had attendants help him out.

sentences.zh: 武禎，宿州臨渙人。

translations.literal: Wu Zhen was a man of Linhuan in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhen came from Linhuan in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖官太史，靖康後業農，後畫界屬金。

translations.literal: His grandfather served as grand astrologer; after the Jingkang era he took up farming; later when the border was drawn [the region] belonged to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather had been a grand astrologer. After the Jingkang debacle the family turned to farming; when the border was later redrawn their district fell under Jin rule.

sentences.zh: 禎深數學。

translations.literal: Zhen was deeply versed in numerology.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was deeply versed in numerology and the calendrical arts.

sentences.zh: 貞祐間，行樞密院僕散安貞聞其名，召至徐州，以上客禮之，每出師必資焉。

translations.literal: During the Zhenyou era, the acting Privy Council Pushe San Anzhen heard his name, summoned him to Xuzhou, treated him with honored-guest ceremony, and on every campaign relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyou era (1213–1217), the acting Privy Councilor Pushe San Anzhen heard of him, summoned him to Xuzhou, received him as an honored guest, and consulted him before every campaign.

sentences.zh: 其占如響。

translations.literal: His divinations were like an echo.
translations.idiomatic: His divinations proved as reliable as an echo.

sentences.zh: 正大初，征至汴京，待詔東華門。

translations.literal: Early in Zhengda he was summoned to Bianjing and attended court at the Donghua Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengda era (1224) he was summoned to Bianjing and attended court at the Donghua Gate.

sentences.zh: 其友王鉉問禎曰：「朝廷若問國祚修短，子何以對？

translations.literal: His friend Wang Xuan asked Zhen: "If the court asks the length of the nation's fortune, how will you answer?
translations.idiomatic: His friend Wang Xuan asked Zhen, "If the court asks how long the dynasty will endure, what will you say?

sentences.zh: 」禎曰：「當以實告之，但更言周過其曆，秦不及期，亦在修德耳。

translations.literal: " Zhen said: "I should tell the truth, but further say that Zhou exceeded its allotted span and Qin did not reach its term—this also lies in cultivating virtue."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhen said, "I must tell the truth—but add that Zhou outlasted its allotted span while Qin fell short of its term, and that fate likewise depends on cultivating virtue."

sentences.zh: 」時久旱祈禱不應，朝廷為憂，禎忽謂鉉曰：「足下今日早歸，恐為雨阻。

translations.literal: " At that time a long drought's prayers went unanswered and the court was worried. Zhen suddenly told Xuan: "You should return home early today—I fear rain will block you.
translations.idiomatic: " A long drought had resisted every prayer, and the court was deeply worried. Zhen suddenly told Xuan, "You should go home early today—I fear rain may hinder your journey."

sentences.zh: 」鉉曰：「萬里無雲，赤日如此，安得有雨？

translations.literal: " Xuan said: "For ten thousand li without a cloud, the red sun like this—how can there be rain?
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan said, "The sky is clear for a thousand li and the sun blazes down—how could it rain?

sentences.zh: 」禎笑曰：「若是，則天不誠也。

translations.literal: " Zhen laughed: "If so, then heaven is not sincere.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhen laughed. "If that were so, heaven would not be sincere."

sentences.zh: 天何嘗不誠。

translations.literal: When has heaven ever not been sincere?
translations.idiomatic: When has heaven ever failed to be sincere?

sentences.zh: 」既而東南有雲氣，須臾蔽天，平地雨注二尺，眾皆驚歎。

translations.literal: " Soon clouds arose in the southeast; in a moment they covered the sky; on the plain rain poured two chi deep—all were startled and sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon clouds rose in the southeast; in a moment they blotted out the sky, and rain fell two chi deep on the plain. Everyone gasped in astonishment.

sentences.zh: 尋除司天臺管勾。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Manager of the Astronomy Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed manager of the Astronomy Bureau.

sentences.zh: 子 亢

translations.literal: Son: Kang
translations.idiomatic: His son Kang

sentences.zh: 子亢，寡言笑，不妄交。

translations.literal: His son Kang spoke little and laughed little, and did not associate rashly.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kang was sparing of speech and laughter and did not make friends lightly.

sentences.zh: 嘗與一學生終日相對，握籌布畫，目炯炯若有所營，見者莫測也。

translations.literal: He once faced a student opposite him for a whole day, holding counting rods and laying out charts, eyes bright as if planning something—those who saw could not fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he sat facing a student all day long, counting rods in hand and charts spread before him, his eyes bright as though engaged in some deep calculation—onlookers could not guess what he was about.

sentences.zh: 哀宗至蔡州，右丞完顏仲德薦其術。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ai reached Caizhou, the Right Vice Chancellor Wanyan Zhongde recommended his arts.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ai reached Caizhou, the Right Vice Chancellor Wanyan Zhongde recommended his arts to the throne.

sentences.zh: 召至，屏人與語，大悅，除司天長行，賞賚甚厚。

translations.literal: He was summoned; others were dismissed to speak with him; [the emperor] was greatly pleased, appointed him Senior Astronomer, and bestowed rewards very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Kang was summoned, attendants were dismissed, and the emperor spoke with him privately. Delighted, Ai appointed him Senior Astronomer and lavished rewards upon him.

sentences.zh: 上書曰：「比者有星變于周、楚之分，彗星起於大角西，掃軫之左軸，蓋除舊佈新之象。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "Recently stars changed in the Zhou and Chu divisions; a comet rose west of the Great Horn and swept the left axle of the Chariot—covering the image of removing the old and spreading the new.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: "Stars have lately shifted in the Zhou and Chu astral divisions; a comet has risen west of the Great Horn and swept the left axle of the Chariot constellation—an omen of casting off the old and setting up the new."

sentences.zh: 」又言：「鄭、楚、週三分野當赤地千里，兵凶大起，王者不可居也。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The three division fields of Zheng, Chu, and Zhou will be red earth for a thousand li; military omens will rise greatly—a king cannot dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "The astral territories of Zheng, Chu, and Zhou will become a thousand li of scorched earth; war omens are rising sharply—a ruler cannot remain there."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「蔡城有兵喪之兆，楚有亡國之征，三軍苦戰於西垣前後有日矣。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Caicheng has omens of army mourning; Chu has the sign of a perishing state; the three armies have bitterly fought before and behind the western wall for days already.
translations.idiomatic: " He added, "Caicheng bears omens of armies and mourning; Chu shows the signs of a state about to perish; our three armies have been fighting desperately before and behind the western wall for days."

sentences.zh: 城壁傾頹，內無見糧，外無應兵，君臣數盡之年也。

translations.literal: The walls are crumbling; inside there is no visible grain; outside there are no responding armies—it is the year when ruler and ministers' allotted spans are exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The walls are crumbling; within there is no grain in sight; without there are no armies to answer our call—it is the year in which the fated spans of ruler and ministers are spent."

sentences.zh: 」聞者悚然奪氣，哀宗惟嗟歎良久，不以此罪。

translations.literal: " Those who heard were startled and their breath was taken; Emperor Ai only sighed for a long while and did not punish him for this.
translations.idiomatic: " Those who heard him were shaken and breathless. Emperor Ai only sighed for a long while and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 性頗倨傲，朝士以此非之。

translations.literal: His nature was quite arrogant; court gentlemen criticized him for this.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature rather arrogant, and court officials faulted him for it.

sentences.zh: 天興二年九月，蔡州被圍，亢奏曰：「十二月三日必攻城。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianxing, ninth month, when Caizhou was besieged, Kang memorialized: "On the third day of the twelfth month they will certainly attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year of Tianxing (1233), when Caizhou was besieged, Kang memorialized, "On the third day of the twelfth month the enemy will certainly assault the city."

sentences.zh: 」及期果然。

translations.literal: " When the date came, it was truly so.
translations.idiomatic: " When the day arrived, it proved true.

sentences.zh: 末帝問曰：「解圍當在何日？

translations.literal: The Last Emperor asked: "On what day will the siege be lifted?
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor asked, "When will the siege be lifted?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「明年正月十三日，城下無一人一騎矣。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Next year, first month, thirteenth day—below the walls there will not be one man or one horse.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "On the thirteenth day of the first month next year there will not be a single man or horse below the walls."

sentences.zh: 」帝不知其由，乃喜圍解有期，日但密計糧草，使可給至其日不闕者。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not know the reason and thus rejoiced that the siege had a date to be lifted; daily he only secretly calculated grain and fodder so supplies could last until that day without shortage.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor did not grasp his meaning and rejoiced that relief was at hand. Day after day he secretly calculated grain and fodder so that supplies would last until that date.

sentences.zh: 明年甲午正月十日，蔡州破，十三日，大元兵退。

translations.literal: Next year, jiawu year, first month, tenth day, Caizhou fell; thirteenth day, the Great Yuan armies withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on the tenth day of the first month of the jiawu year (1234), Caizhou fell; on the thirteenth day the armies of the Great Yuan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是日，亢赴水死雲。

translations.literal: That day Kang threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: That day Kang drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 李懋，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Li Mao—of unknown origin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mao—his place of origin is unknown.

sentences.zh: 有異術。

translations.literal: He had extraordinary arts.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed extraordinary arts.

sentences.zh: 正大間，遊京兆，行省完顏合達愛其術，與俱至汴京，薦于哀宗。

translations.literal: During Zhengda he traveled in Jingzhao; the Branch Secretariat Wanyan Heda loved his arts, went with him to Bianjing, and recommended him to Emperor Ai.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengda era he traveled in the Jingzhao region. The branch secretariat official Wanyan Heda admired his arts, accompanied him to Bianjing, and recommended him to Emperor Ai.

sentences.zh: 遣近侍密問國運否泰，言無忌避。

translations.literal: [The emperor] sent personal attendants to ask secretly whether the national fortune was good or ill; he spoke without taboo or avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent personal attendants to ask him privately about the dynasty's fortunes, and Mao spoke without reserve or evasion.

sentences.zh: 居之繁台寺，朝士日走問之，或能道隱事及吉凶之變，人以為神。

translations.literal: He dwelt at the Fantai Temple; court gentlemen daily came running to ask him—he could sometimes tell hidden matters and changes of fortune and misfortune; people thought him a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He lodged at the Fantai Temple, and court officials flocked to him daily. He could sometimes reveal hidden affairs and foretell changes of fortune and misfortune, and people regarded him as supernatural.

sentences.zh: 帝惡其言太泄，遣使者殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor hated that his words leaked too much and sent an envoy to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor resented how freely he spoke and sent an envoy to kill him.

sentences.zh: 使者乃持酒肴入寺，懋出迎，笑曰：「是矣。

translations.literal: The envoy came bearing wine and delicacies into the temple; Mao came out to welcome him and laughed: "It is this.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy arrived at the temple bearing wine and food. Mao came out to greet him and smiled. "So it has come to this."

sentences.zh: 」使者曰：「何謂也？

translations.literal: " The envoy said: "What do you mean?
translations.idiomatic: " The envoy asked, "What do you mean?"

sentences.zh: 」懋曰：「我數當盡今日，尚複何言。

translations.literal: " Mao said: "My allotted span should end today—what more is there to say?
translations.idiomatic: " Mao said, "My fated span ends today—what more is there to say?"

sentences.zh: 」遂索酒，痛飲就死。

translations.literal: " He then sought wine, drank heavily, and met death.
translations.idiomatic: " He called for wine, drank deeply, and died.

sentences.zh: 胡德新

translations.literal: Hu Dexin
translations.idiomatic: Hu Dexin

sentences.zh: 胡德新，河北士族也。

translations.literal: Hu Dexin was of a Hebei gentry clan.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Dexin came from a gentry family of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 寓居南陽，往來宛、葉間，嗜酒落魄不羈，言禍福有奇驗。

translations.literal: He lodged at Nanyang, traveled between Wan and Ye, loved wine and was unrestrained and unbridled—speaking of fortune and calamity he had strange verification.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at Nanyang and traveled between Wan and Ye. Fond of wine, he was down-at-heel and unbridled, yet when he spoke of fortune and calamity his words were uncannily borne out.

sentences.zh: 正大七年夏，與燕人王鉉邂逅於葉縣村落中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhengda, summer, he met by chance the Yan man Wang Xuan in a village of Ye county.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the seventh year of Zhengda (1230) he happened upon Wang Xuan of Yan in a village of Ye county.

sentences.zh: 與鉉初不相識，坐中謬以兵官對，胡曰：「此公在吾法中當登科甲，何以謂之兵官。

translations.literal: He and Xuan did not know each other at first; in the gathering [someone] wrongly addressed [Xuan] as a military officer. Hu said: "This gentleman in my art should ascend to jinshi rank—why call him a military officer?
translations.idiomatic: They were strangers at first. Someone at the gathering mistakenly addressed Xuan as a military officer. Hu said, "By my art this gentleman is destined to pass the jinshi examination—why call him a soldier?

sentences.zh: 」眾愕然，遂以實告。

translations.literal: " All were startled and then told the truth.
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone was astonished, and they then told him the truth.

sentences.zh: 二人相得甚歡，即命家人具雞酒以待，酒酣、舉大白相屬曰：「君此去事業甚遠，不必置問。

translations.literal: The two got along very happily and immediately ordered the household to prepare chicken and wine to wait on them; when wine was merry they raised a large cup to each other, saying: "Your going from here—your career is very far; there is no need to place questions.
translations.idiomatic: The two took to each other at once. Hu had his household prepare chicken and wine. When they were well into their cups he raised a full goblet and said, "Your career from here will be a long one—do not trouble yourself with questions."

sentences.zh: 某有所見，久不敢對人言，今欲告子。

translations.literal: I have some observation I long dared not speak to people—now I wish to tell you.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen something I have long dared not tell anyone—now I wish to confide it to you."

sentences.zh: 」遂邀至野田，密謂曰：「某自去年來，行宛、葉道中，見往來者十且八九有死氣。

translations.literal: " He then invited him to the wild fields and secretly said: "I since last year on the roads between Wan and Ye have seen travelers—nine or eight of ten have death qi.
translations.idiomatic: " He then led Xuan into the open fields and said in secret, "Since last year, on the roads between Wan and Ye, I have seen that nine travelers in ten bear the aura of death."

sentences.zh: 今春至陳、許間，見其人亦有大半當死者。

translations.literal: This spring reaching the Chen and Xu region, I see among the people also more than half should die.
translations.idiomatic: This spring, in the region between Chen and Xu, I see that more than half the people there are likewise marked for death."

sentences.zh: 若吾目可用，則時事可知矣。

translations.literal: If my eyes can be trusted, then current affairs can be known.
translations.idiomatic: If my eyes can be trusted, the course of events is plain to see."

sentences.zh: 」鉉驚問應驗遲速，曰：「不過歲月間耳，某亦不逃此厄，請密志之。

translations.literal: " Xuan startled asked when verification would come, fast or slow; [Hu] said: "Not passing beyond months—and I also cannot escape this calamity; please secretly note it.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan asked in alarm how soon this would come to pass. Hu said, "Within a few months—and I shall not escape the calamity either. Please keep this to yourself."

sentences.zh: 」明年，大元兵由金、房入，取峭石灘渡漢，所過廬舍蕭然，胡亦舉家及難，其精驗如此。

translations.literal: " Next year the Great Yuan armies entered by Jin and Fang, took the Qiaoshi ford to cross the Han—wherever they passed dwellings were desolate; Hu also with his whole family met disaster—his precision verified thus.
translations.idiomatic: " The next year the armies of the Great Yuan entered through Jin and Fang, crossed the Han at the Qiaoshi ford, and left every dwelling they passed desolate. Hu and his whole family perished in the disaster—his foresight verified just so.
